4. That, in the circumstances, the petitioner reduced total number of seats of the Hall from 1023 to 703 with effect from 4-7-1985. And accordingly wrote to the Customs authority for grant of the permission. But the authority of Customs and Excise, Jessore sat over the matter for a long time for nearly 15 months and ultimately on 9-11-86 approval was given to the reduction of seats as prayed for. That dispute arose between the petitioner and the Customs authority of Jessore with regard to payment of Capacity Tax for the period 4-7-1985 to 8-11-1986, that is, the period in between the submission of application to the Customs authority and date of accord of permission for the reduction of seats. The said permission was ultimately accorded to for the reduction of seats on 9-11-1986 by the authority of Customs and Excise, Jessore. But an Assistant Collector of Customs duly signed the Register maintained for the purpose of capacity Tax since the date of reduction of seats/Capacity unilaterally by the petitioner. It has been further stated in the petition that because of establishment of another big Cinema Hall in the heart of Jessore town there was fall of business of the petitioner which compelled the petitioner to reduce the number of seats of the Cinema Hall. The Customs authority, although, was fully aware of the fact of reduction of seats demanded the payment of Capacity Tax on the basis of computation of original 1023 seats without taking into notice that the petitioner on and from 4-7-1985 had already reduced the number of seats to 703. 

 10. Mr. Sheikh Razzaque Ali, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the demand of Customs authority pertaining to arrear of dues with penalty is illegal, malafide in that the petitioner having faced the business difficulties and financial stringency in payment of bank loan intimated the customs authority in clear terms on 4-7-1985 that the seats of the Cinema Hall has been reduced to 703 from 1023 and that Assistant Collector of Customs had been verifying the register of the Cinema Hall every day where he put his signature and thus was fully aware of the number of seats and, number of shows in each day of the Cinema Hall. That as evident from Annexure-C-3 to the writ petition, he further submitted that certain papers and documents were asked from the petitioner by the Customs authority though those could not be produced in time was ultimately made over to the authority. But it seems without considering and perusing any document the authority from 4-7-1985 to 8-11-1986 in a malafide and arbitrary manner sat over the mauer causing financial prejudice to the petitioner. And ultimately on 9-11-1986 the permission as sought for the reduction of seats was accorded to the petitioner. The learned Counsel strenuously argued that the petitioner should be exempted from the payment of the additional duty with interest and penalty. And as for the arrear dues the petitioner is prepared to deposit the same. Further submission of the learned Counsel is that the concept of fairness demands that the matter in the hand of the executive authority be disposed of as expeditiously as possible although there is no time prescribed for that in the statues. The learned Counsel in this regard also stressed on the principle of legitimate expectation of a citizen and lastly, he invoked the principles of Audi Alterum Partem that is to say natural justice in matter of fixing the financial burden of the petitioner. The learned Counsel placed his reliance in a decision reported in 21 DLR (SC) 225 a case under Article 98 of 1962 Constitution of Pakistan which deals with locus-standi of a petitioner. Reliance has also been placed in a case reported in 46 DLR 282 wherein the similar question of standing was decided by a Division Bench of the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh under Article 102 of the Constitution. In both the cases cited before us the moot point is that of locus-standi and the high principles of maintaining a proceeding by a person having sufficient interest in the matter against action of an executive authority who has legal duty to perform and discharge his duties in a manner permitted by law so to do. These celebrated principles are universally accepted in the constitutional jurisprudence in matters of judicial review of administrative action or quasi judicial' action/proceeding and, as such, there is no dispute about that.
